# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 2 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 2:1 — title for Joseph: "Powerful One" vs. "Mighty One" vs. "champion"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Joseph the Powerful-One of God" | Hyphenated compound; literal Greek dynatos |
| LOGOS | "Joseph, the Mighty One of God" | Standard formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "Joseph — God's champion" | Functional; loses the divine-attribute structure |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "Mighty One of God." PNEUMA's "champion" reframes the epithet as an achievement rather than an attribute. EMET's hyphenation is syntactically awkward as a title.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:2 — reason Joseph avoids women: "foreign" vs. "strange" vs. implied

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "any woman who is a stranger" | Literal allotrian |
| LOGOS | "any foreign woman" | Standard translation |
| PNEUMA | "strange women" | Slightly archaic in this usage |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "foreign woman." The Greek allotria means "belonging to another" — not merely unknown but outside his people.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:12 — Aseneth's soliloquy: "wretched" vs. "miserable" vs. omitted self-description

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "miserable-woman that I am" | Literal talaipōros with hyphen |
| LOGOS | "wretched as I am" | Formal, natural English |
| PNEUMA | omits self-condemnation | Smooths narrative, loses self-awareness beat |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The self-condemnation is important: it marks the beginning of Aseneth's recognition of her arrogance. PNEUMA's omission removes this narrative function.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Narratologically significant.

---
